AKBAYAN SLAMS CONTRACTORS, SAYS PEOPLE'S TAXES ARE NOT FOR LUXURY

Akbayan Partylist staged a protest Friday at St. Gerrard Construction, one of the top 15 contractors that cornered 20% of the government's flood control budget, accusing it of involvement in substandard or even non-existent projects. The firm, owned by Sara Discaya—recently exposed for flaunting a lavish lifestyle—has become a symbol of how public funds are misused, the group said.

Deputy Minority Leader and Akbayan Rep. Perci Cendaña denounced contractors like the Discayas for squandering taxpayers' money. "The widespread uproar and condemnation of such flagrant displays of wealth by the likes of Discaya is deserved. But more than condemnation—dapat kasuhan at ikulong ang mga nangungulimbat ng buwis ng mamamayan."

He also took a swipe at Discaya's ostentation: "Kagaya nung isang katukayo niya, itong Sarah D hindi rin tinamaan ng hiya sa pag-flex ng mga luho. Hindi inspirational ang pangungulimbat. Hindi po pang FYP ang inyong na-SOP sa korapsyon."

Cendaña lauded netizens for helping expose corruption and urged the revival of the mandatory publication of officials' Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs) as a deterrent. "We should embrace the moral outrage of our citizens. Kasama ang mamamayan sa pagsugpo ng katiwalian—hindi sila tagasubaybay lang."

Matthew Silverio, secretary general of the Student Council Alliance of the Philippines, echoed the youth's frustration, saying public money wasted on ghost projects could have transformed lives. "Habang milyon-milyon ang nalulunod sa baha at walang maayos na paaralan, may mga kontratista namang nalulunod sa luho."

He stressed that the fight against corruption is about the nation's future: "The money that was stolen could have gone to building classrooms, hiring more teachers, and securing a better future for the next generation Hindi lang ito usapin ng flood control projects na hindi makita—ito ay usapin ng kinabukasan ng kabataan at ng bayan."
